## P1: Mobile agents and agent/process migration

### AMP-007

Tomas Sander, Christian F. Tschudin (1998). **Protecting Mobile Agents Against Malicious Hosts**. *Mobile Agents and Security, G. Vigna (ed.), Lecture Notes in Computer Science vol. 1419, Springer, pp. 44-60*. [doi:10.1007/3-540-68671-1_4](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-68671-1_4). Cite key: `sander1998protecting`.

The chapter addresses the problem that a mobile agent executing on an untrusted host is exposed to that host. It proposes software-only techniques for computing with encrypted functions so that a host can run a mobile code fragment that evaluates a polynomial without learning what it computes. It also describes how an agent can digitally sign its output securely.

- **Relevance:** It frames the core trust problem of relocating an agent onto infrastructure its owner does not control, which applies directly to moving LLM agents across organizations.
- **Operations:** identity-trust, runtime-relocation. **Contribution:** formal. **Type:** book-chapter (not peer reviewed).
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Edited collection (ed. G. Vigna); formal peer review of chapters not verifiable, so marked not peer-reviewed conservatively. Abstract withheld by publisher; summary checked against the abstract as reproduced by BibBase.

### AMP-008

Alfonso Fuggetta, Gian Pietro Picco, Giovanni Vigna (1998). **Understanding code mobility**. *IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering*. [doi:10.1109/32.685258](https://doi.org/10.1109/32.685258). Cite key: `fuggetta1998understanding`.

The paper argues that research on mobile code lacked a shared vocabulary, which made existing approaches hard to compare. It proposes a conceptual framework that classifies code mobility along three dimensions: technologies, design paradigms and applications. It reviews the state of the art through this lens, offers guidelines for choosing paradigms and implementation technologies, and illustrates the classification with a case study.

- **Relevance:** Its classification of what moves (code, execution state, data) and of the design paradigms is the standard vocabulary for distinguishing relocation, remote execution and delegation of agent work.
- **Operations:** runtime-relocation, delegation. **Contribution:** taxonomy. **Type:** journal.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Full author given names taken from OpenAlex; Crossref lists initials. Abstract read via OpenAlex.

### AMP-009

Joachim Baumann, Fritz Hohl, Kurt Rothermel, Markus Straßer (1998). **Mole – Concepts of a mobile agent system**. *World Wide Web*. [doi:10.1023/A:1019211714301](https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1019211714301). Cite key: `baumann1998mole`.

A 1998 article in the World Wide Web journal describing the concepts behind Mole, a mobile agent system developed at the University of Stuttgart. The title indicates a conceptual account of how the system supports mobile agents. Its abstract and full text could not be reached during verification, so no specific design claims are made here.

- **Relevance:** An early mobile agent system design from the University of Stuttgart, useful as historical background on how agent platforms approached moving running agents between hosts.
- **Operations:** runtime-relocation, delegation, identity-trust. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** journal.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Publisher withholds the abstract and the full text was not reachable during audit; summary kept deliberately generic. Crossref lists author initials; first names come from OpenAlex and University of Stuttgart records. WWW journal vol. 1, no. 3, pp. 123-137.

### AMP-011

Danny B. Lange, Mitsuru Oshima (1999). **Seven good reasons for mobile agents**. *Communications of the ACM*. [doi:10.1145/295685.298136](https://doi.org/10.1145/295685.298136). Cite key: `lange1999seven`.

This two-page Communications of the ACM article argues for mobile agents, which are programs that can move themselves between hosts on a network so they can work next to the resources they use. Secondary sources say it gives seven motivations: lower network load, tolerance of network latency, encapsulation of protocols, asynchronous and autonomous execution, dynamic adaptation, heterogeneity, and robustness and fault tolerance. The full text was not retrieved for this audit.

- **Relevance:** It states the original reasons for moving an agent to where the work is, which is the baseline that any argument for relocating LLM agents must answer.
- **Operations:** runtime-relocation, delegation. **Contribution:** position. **Type:** journal.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: No abstract indexed (Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar); ACM PDF blocked during audit. List of reasons taken from secondary sources, not re-read from the full text. Pages 88-89.

### AMP-012

Wayne Jansen, Tom Karygiannis (1999). **Mobile agent security**. *NIST Special Publication 800-19, National Institute of Standards and Technology*. [doi:10.6028/nist.sp.800-19](https://doi.org/10.6028/nist.sp.800-19). Cite key: `jansen1999mobile`.

This NIST report describes mobile agents as programs that suspend execution on one host, transfer themselves to another agent-enabled host and resume there. It surveys the threats faced by designers of agent platforms and developers of agent applications, including threats from agents to platforms and from platforms to agents. It identifies generic security objectives and a range of countermeasures for them.

- **Relevance:** It provides a threat model for moving agents between hosts that can be mapped onto cross-organization LLM agent handoff and relocation.
- **Operations:** identity-trust, runtime-relocation, governance. **Contribution:** survey. **Type:** tech-report (not peer reviewed).
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Abstract read from the NIST CSRC publication page, which gives the date as October 1999 (month only). Threat categories (agent-to-platform, agent-to-agent, platform-to-agent, other-to-agent-platform) confirmed in the report PDF. NIST withdrew SP 800-19 on 2018-08-01 as outdated.

### AMP-013

Dejan S. Milojičić, Fred Douglis, Yves Paindaveine, Richard Wheeler, Songnian Zhou (2000). **Process migration**. *ACM Computing Surveys, vol. 32, no. 3, pp. 241-299*. [doi:10.1145/367701.367728](https://doi.org/10.1145/367701.367728). Cite key: `milojicic2000process`.

This survey defines process migration as moving a running process between machines, which supports load distribution, fault resilience, easier administration and data locality. It reviews the key concepts and analyzes design and implementation issues, then revisits them through case studies of MOSIX, Sprite, Mach and Load Sharing Facility. It focuses on practical matters and on why migration had not been widely adopted.

- **Relevance:** It catalogs the residual-dependency, state-transfer and transparency problems that recur when an agent's running state is moved between machines.
- **Operations:** runtime-relocation. **Contribution:** survey. **Type:** journal.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Abstract read via OpenAlex.

### AMP-014

Robert S. Gray, George Cybenko, David Kotz, Ronald A. Peterson, Daniela Rus (2002). **D'Agents: Applications and performance of a mobile-agent system**. *Software: Practice and Experience*. [doi:10.1002/spe.449](https://doi.org/10.1002/spe.449). Cite key: `gray2002d`.

The paper presents D'Agents, a general-purpose mobile-agent system descended from Agent Tcl, and an information-retrieval application for military field personnel. It explains how D'Agents differs from most systems by supporting strong mobility and several agent languages. Using a small representative retrieval application, it compares the scalability of mobile agents with client/server approaches and finds that the results confirm and quantify when mobile code is useful.

- **Relevance:** It gives empirical evidence on when moving an agent with its execution state outperforms remote calls, which informs when LLM agent relocation is worth its cost.
- **Operations:** runtime-relocation, delegation. **Contribution:** empirical. **Type:** journal.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Abstract read via OpenAlex.

### AMP-015

Christopher Clark, Keir Fraser, Steven Hand, Jacob Gorm Hansen, Eric Jul, Christian Limpach, Ian Pratt, Andrew Warfield (2005). **Live Migration of Virtual Machines**. *2nd Symposium on Networked Systems Design & Implementation (NSDI 05), USENIX Association*. <https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi-05/live-migration-virtual-machines>. Cite key: `clark2005live`.

The paper studies how to move whole operating-system instances between physical hosts while they keep serving requests, for fault management, load balancing and maintenance. It introduces the writable working set concept and presents the design, implementation and evaluation of iterative live migration built on the Xen VMM. On a commodity cluster it reports service downtimes as low as 60 ms, which makes live migration practical even for interactive server workloads.

- **Relevance:** Pre-copy live migration is the reference technique for relocating a running workload with minimal downtime, and agent-runtime relocation reuses its ideas.
- **Operations:** runtime-relocation. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** publisher. Note: No DOI; USENIX proceedings, NSDI '05 pp. 273-286. Metadata and abstract come from the USENIX landing page and the paper PDF. DBLP was rate-limited during verification.

### AMP-018

Carlo Puliafito, Carlo Vallati, Enzo Mingozzi, Giovanni Merlino, Francesco Longo, Antonio Puliafito (2019). **Container Migration in the Fog: A Performance Evaluation**. *Sensors*. [doi:10.3390/s19071488](https://doi.org/10.3390/s19071488). Cite key: `puliafito2019container`.

The paper studies container migration between fog nodes for IoT use cases such as smart transportation and smart industry. It reviews cold, pre-copy, post-copy and hybrid container migration techniques and evaluates them extensively on a real fog computing testbed. The results show which technique is most appropriate under different network and service conditions.

- **Relevance:** Containers are the usual sandbox for LLM agents, so a measured comparison of container migration strategies applies directly to checkpointing and relocating agent runtimes.
- **Operations:** runtime-relocation. **Contribution:** empirical. **Type:** journal.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Abstract read via OpenAlex. The abstract does not name the checkpoint tool (CRIU was not confirmed).

### AMP-035

Biao Sun, Ziming Huang, Hanyu Zhao, Wencong Xiao, Xinyi Zhang, Yong Li, Wei Lin (2024). **Llumnix: Dynamic Scheduling for Large Language Model Serving**. *18th USENIX Symposium on Operating Systems Design and Implementation (OSDI 24)*. [arXiv:2406.03243](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.03243). Cite key: `sun2024llumnix`.

Llumnix targets LLM serving workloads whose requests vary unpredictably in resource and latency needs, which causes queuing delays and SLO violations. Like context switching across CPU cores, it reschedules requests across model instances at runtime using a scalable live migration mechanism for requests and their in-memory state, driven by a unified dynamic scheduling policy. The evaluation reports an order-of-magnitude improvement in tail latency, up to 1.5x faster high-priority requests, and up to 36% cost savings at similar tail latency.

- **Relevance:** It shows that the in-flight state of an LLM inference (its KV cache) can be migrated live between instances, which is the model-layer counterpart of relocating an agent.
- **Operations:** runtime-relocation. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** publisher. Note: Venue and authors from the USENIX OSDI '24 landing page (first page 173; ISBN 978-1-939133-40-3); also arXiv 2406.03243. Month is the OSDI conference month. No DOI.

### AMP-048

Radostin Stoyanov, Viktória Spišaková, Jesus Ramos, Steven Gurfinkel, Andrei Vagin, Adrian Reber, Wesley Armour, Rodrigo Bruno (2025). **CRIUgpu: Transparent Checkpointing of GPU-Accelerated Workloads**. *arXiv*. [arXiv:2502.16631](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16631). Cite key: `stoyanov2025criugpu`.

The paper addresses checkpointing of large GPU workloads that are often preempted or interrupted on shared clusters. Instead of intercepting and replaying device API calls, CRIUgpu builds on recent GPU driver capabilities to take transparent, unified CPU and GPU snapshots for CUDA and ROCm applications through CRIU. The evaluation on deep learning and HPC workloads across multiple GPUs shows no steady-state overhead and much shorter recovery times than prior transparent GPU checkpointing.

- **Relevance:** It extends CRIU-based checkpoint/restore to GPU state, a prerequisite for relocating agents that host local models or GPU tools.
- **Operations:** runtime-relocation. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** preprint (not peer reviewed).
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: Preprint; no peer-reviewed venue was found in the arXiv record.

### AMP-056

Xingdan Wang, Jiayi He, Zhiqing Tang, Jianxiong Guo, Jiong Lou, Liping Qian, Tian Wang, Weijia Jia (2025). **Adaptive AI Agent Placement and Migration in Edge Intelligence Systems**. *2025 IEEE 25th International Conference on Communication Technology (ICCT), pp. 1475-1480*. [doi:10.1109/icct67417.2025.11373977](https://doi.org/10.1109/icct67417.2025.11373977). Cite key: `wang2025adaptive`.

The paper deals with deploying LLM-based agents on resource-limited, heterogeneous edge servers. Keeping service quality for mobile users requires migrating these agents, which is complicated because each agent coordinates LLMs, task planning, memory and external tools. The authors propose an adaptive placement and migration framework that models resource, latency and cost constraints and decides with ant colony algorithms plus LLM-based optimisation. Migration is kept lightweight by moving only essential state. A prototype built on AgentScope and tested on globally distributed edge servers is reported to cut deployment latency and migration cost substantially.

- **Relevance:** It is a direct modern case of mobile agents for LLMs, in which an agent's essential state is moved between edge hosts.
- **Operations:** runtime-relocation, portable-context. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: Peer-reviewed version in IEEE ICCT 2025 (Shenyang, 16-18 Oct 2025), found by Crossref title search; it has the same title, authors and abstract as arXiv 2508.03345 (posted 2025-08-05).

### AMP-070

Yusheng Zheng, Yiwei Yang, Wei Zhang, Andi Quinn (2026). **ACRFence: Preventing Semantic Rollback Attacks in Agent Checkpoint-Restore**. *arXiv (journal_ref: CoDAIM workshop 2026)*. [arXiv:2603.20625](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.20625). Cite key: `zheng2026acrfence`.

The paper shows that checkpoint-restore in LLM agent frameworks is unsafe because, after a restore, an agent re-generates tool requests that differ slightly from the originals, so servers treat them as new. The authors define this as semantic rollback attacks, identify two classes (Action Replay and Authority Resurrection), and validate them in a proof of concept. They propose ACRFence, a framework-agnostic mitigation that records irreversible tool effects and enforces replay-or-fork semantics on restore.

- **Relevance:** It identifies a safety failure unique to resuming LLM agents from checkpoints, which is central to runtime relocation without loss of accountability.
- **Operations:** runtime-relocation, tool-access, identity-trust. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** preprint (not peer reviewed).
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: The arXiv journal_ref names the CoDAIM workshop 2026, but the workshop proceedings were not confirmed, so it is marked as a preprint and not peer-reviewed.


## P2: Agent communication protocols and interoperability

### AMP-003

Thomas R. Gruber (1993). **A translation approach to portable ontology specifications**. *Knowledge Acquisition*. [doi:10.1006/knac.1993.1008](https://doi.org/10.1006/knac.1993.1008). Cite key: `gruber1993translation`.

Defines an ontology as a specification of a shared representational vocabulary and addresses how such vocabularies can be shared and reused across different knowledge representation systems. Ontolingua lets ontologies be written once in a standard predicate-calculus format and translated into several specialised representation systems, so knowledge can be shared without giving up the efficiency of each implementation.

- **Relevance:** Semantic portability of shared vocabularies is a prerequisite for task context that keeps its meaning when moved across agent frameworks.
- **Operations:** portable-context, cross-framework-migration. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** journal.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Abstract read via Semantic Scholar; metadata from Crossref.

### AMP-004

Tim Finin, Richard Fritzson, Don McKay, Robin McEntire (1994). **KQML as an agent communication language**. *Proceedings of the Third International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM '94)*. [doi:10.1145/191246.191322](https://doi.org/10.1145/191246.191322). Cite key: `finin1994kqml`.

Introduces KQML, developed within the ARPA Knowledge Sharing Effort, as both a message format and a message-handling protocol so that independently built software agents can exchange knowledge at run time. Messages are typed by performatives (e.g., ask, tell) that are independent of the content language, and special facilitator agents provide routing and brokering between agents.

- **Relevance:** KQML's separation of a typed message envelope from its content and its facilitator-mediated routing is the conceptual ancestor of A2A task messages and portable task envelopes.
- **Operations:** delegation, portable-context. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Crossref record lists year only (1994).

### AMP-005

Michael R. Genesereth, Steven P. Ketchpel (1994). **Software agents**. *Communications of the ACM*. [doi:10.1145/176789.176794](https://doi.org/10.1145/176789.176794). Cite key: `genesereth1994software`.

This Communications of the ACM article treats agent-based software engineering as a way to let independently written, heterogeneous programs interoperate by having them exchange messages in a common agent communication language. The language comes out of the DARPA Knowledge Sharing Effort and relates to KIF and KQML. The authors also describe a federation-style architecture for organizing such agents. The full text was not retrieved for this audit, so finer details are not confirmed here.

- **Relevance:** An early proposal to make heterogeneous programs interoperate through a shared agent communication language and a federation architecture, an antecedent of today's protocol-based (MCP/A2A-style) interoperability needed for cross-framework movement.
- **Operations:** delegation, cross-framework-migration. **Contribution:** position. **Type:** journal.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Full text not retrieved during audit (ACM DL blocked; no abstract indexed). Summary limited to what bibliographic records and secondary sources confirm. Pages 48-53 per library catalog.

### AMP-006

M.P. Singh (1998). **Agent communication languages: rethinking the principles**. *Computer (IEEE)*. [doi:10.1109/2.735849](https://doi.org/10.1109/2.735849). Cite key: `singh1998agent`.

Argues that agent communication languages whose semantics rest on agents' private mental states (beliefs, intentions) cannot be verified in open, heterogeneous systems. Proposes instead grounding ACL semantics in publicly observable social commitments among agents.

- **Relevance:** Commitment-based semantics give a verifiable notion of who owes what after a handoff, directly relevant to preserving accountability when work moves between agents.
- **Operations:** delegation, governance. **Contribution:** position. **Type:** journal.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Crossref gives author as 'M.P. Singh' (Munindar P. Singh); year only.

### AMP-010

Yannis Labrou, Tim Finin, Yun Peng (1999). **Agent communication languages: the current landscape**. *IEEE Intelligent Systems*. [doi:10.1109/5254.757631](https://doi.org/10.1109/5254.757631). Cite key: `labrou1999agent`.

Reviews the state of agent communication languages at the end of the 1990s, focusing on KQML and the FIPA ACL. It compares their message structure, performatives and approaches to formal semantics, and discusses open issues such as conversation policies and the practical adoption of ACL standards.

- **Relevance:** Gives the baseline comparison of the two classic ACL standards against which modern LLM agent protocols (A2A, ACP, ANP) can be positioned.
- **Operations:** delegation. **Contribution:** survey. **Type:** journal.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Author names given as initials in Crossref (Yannis Labrou, Tim Finin).

### AMP-038

Samuele Marro, Emanuele La Malfa, Jesse Wright, Guohao Li, Nigel Shadbolt, Michael Wooldridge, Philip Torr (2024). **A Scalable Communication Protocol for Networks of Large Language Models**. *arXiv preprint*. [arXiv:2410.11905](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11905). Cite key: `marro2024scalable`.

Identifies an 'Agent Communication Trilemma' between versatility, efficiency and portability in large networks of LLM agents. Proposes Agora, a meta-protocol in which agents use standardised routines for frequent exchanges, natural language for rare ones, and LLM-written routines in between. The authors report that Agora copes with changing interfaces and members and that self-organising automated protocols emerge in large networks.

- **Relevance:** Shows how agents can negotiate and evolve protocols on the fly, relevant to interoperating across frameworks that do not share a fixed message schema.
- **Operations:** delegation, cross-framework-migration. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** preprint (not peer reviewed).
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: OpenReview lists an ICLR 2025 submission that was withdrawn; treated as preprint.

### AMP-041

Weize Chen, Ziming You, Ran Li, Yitong Guan, Chen Qian, Chenyang Zhao, Cheng Yang, Ruobing Xie, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun (2025). **Internet of Agents: Weaving a Web of Heterogeneous Agents for Collaborative Intelligence**. *International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2025)*. [arXiv:2407.07061](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.07061). Cite key: `chen2025internet`.

Observes that existing LLM multi-agent frameworks struggle to integrate third-party agents, are mostly single-device, and rely on hard-coded communication pipelines. Proposes the Internet of Agents, with an agent integration protocol, an instant-messaging-style architecture, and dynamic agent teaming and conversation-flow control. Experiments on general assistant, embodied AI and RAG benchmarks show it outperforming prior baselines.

- **Relevance:** Demonstrates distributed, protocol-based teaming of heterogeneous agents across devices, a concrete substrate for handing work between agents from different ecosystems.
- **Operations:** delegation, cross-framework-migration. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** publisher. Note: arXiv first posted 2024-07-09; ICLR 2025 (Spotlight) confirmed on OpenReview.

### AMP-050

Yingxuan Yang, Huacan Chai, Yuanyi Song, Siyuan Qi, Muning Wen, Ning Li, Junwei Liao, Haoyi Hu, Jianghao Lin, Gaowei Chang, Weiwen Liu, Ying Wen, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang (2025). **A Survey of AI Agent Protocols**. *arXiv preprint*. [arXiv:2504.16736](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.16736). Cite key: `yang2025survey`.

Argues that the lack of a standard way for LLM agents to talk to tools and to each other limits collaboration and scale. Surveys existing agent protocols using a two-dimensional classification (context-oriented vs. inter-agent; general-purpose vs. domain-specific), compares them on dimensions such as security, scalability and latency, and outlines properties needed in next-generation protocols such as adaptability and privacy preservation.

- **Relevance:** Provides a taxonomy that separates tool-access protocols from inter-agent delegation protocols, mirroring the corpus's split between MCP-style tool access and A2A-style handoff.
- **Operations:** delegation, tool-access, identity-trust. **Contribution:** survey. **Type:** preprint (not peer reviewed).
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv.

### AMP-051

Abul Ehtesham, Aditi Singh, Gaurav Kumar Gupta, Saket Kumar (2025). **A survey of agent interoperability protocols: Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent Communication Protocol (ACP), Agent-to-Agent Protocol (A2A), and Agent Network Protocol (ANP)**. *arXiv preprint*. [arXiv:2505.02279](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.02279). Cite key: `ehtesham2025survey`.

Compares four emerging LLM agent protocols: MCP (JSON-RPC client-server tool invocation), ACP (RESTful, MIME-typed multipart messaging), A2A (peer-to-peer task delegation via capability-based Agent Cards) and ANP (open-network discovery using W3C DIDs and JSON-LD). The protocols are contrasted on interaction modes, discovery, communication patterns and security, and a phased adoption path is suggested.

- **Relevance:** Directly maps which protocol handles tool access, delegation and decentralized identity, the building blocks for moving tasks between agents and organizations.
- **Operations:** delegation, tool-access, identity-trust. **Contribution:** survey. **Type:** preprint (not peer reviewed).
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv.

### AMP-052

Ken Huang, Vineeth Sai Narajala, Idan Habler, Akram Sheriff (2026). **Agent Name Service (ANS): A Universal Directory for Secure AI Agent Discovery and Interoperability**. *2026 IEEE 5th International Conference on AI in Cybersecurity (ICAIC)*. [doi:10.1109/icaic67076.2026.11395757](https://doi.org/10.1109/icaic67076.2026.11395757). Cite key: `huang2026agent`.

Addresses the absence of a public discovery framework for AI agents by proposing ANS, a DNS-inspired, protocol-agnostic registry. ANS uses PKI certificates for verifiable agent identity, defines registration and renewal for lifecycle management, supports capability-aware name resolution, and adds a protocol adapter layer for A2A, MCP and ACP; the paper includes a threat analysis.

- **Relevance:** Discovery and verifiable naming determine how a delegating agent finds and trusts the agent that receives moved work.
- **Operations:** identity-trust, delegation. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: Published at IEEE ICAIC 2026 (Houston, 18-20 Feb 2026, pp. 1-9; Crossref). arXiv 2505.10609 (2025-05-15) preprint; its comment states endorsement by the OWASP GenAI ASI Project. Citekey retains the arXiv year.

### AMP-055

Mohammed Mehedi Hasan, Hao Li, Emad Fallahzadeh, Gopi Krishnan Rajbahadur, Bram Adams, Ahmed E. Hassan (2026). **Model Context Protocol (MCP) at First Glance: Studying the Security and Maintainability of MCP Servers**. *ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology (TOSEM)*. [doi:10.1145/3814959](https://doi.org/10.1145/3814959). Cite key: `hasan2026model`.

Presents a large-scale empirical study of 1,899 open-source MCP servers, combining project health metrics with general-purpose static analysis and an MCP-specific scanner. Servers score well on health metrics but the study identifies eight distinct vulnerability types, only three of which overlap with traditional software vulnerabilities, including MCP-specific tool poisoning; 7.2% of servers have general vulnerabilities and 5.5% show tool poisoning, and code smells are common.

- **Relevance:** Provides empirical evidence on the quality and safety of the MCP server ecosystem that agents depend on when their tool access moves with them.
- **Operations:** tool-access, governance. **Contribution:** empirical. **Type:** journal.
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: Published in ACM TOSEM (article 3814959, online 2026-05-12; volume/issue not yet assigned in Crossref). arXiv 2506.13538 first posted 2025-06-16; citekey retains 2025.


## P3: Security of LLM agents, tool use and multi-agent handoffs

### AMP-025

Kai Greshake, Sahar Abdelnabi, Shailesh Mishra, Christoph Endres, Thorsten Holz, Mario Fritz (2023). **Not What You've Signed Up For: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection**. *Proceedings of the 16th ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security (AISec '23, co-located with ACM CCS 2023)*. [doi:10.1145/3605764.3623985](https://doi.org/10.1145/3605764.3623985). Cite key: `greshake2023not`.

The paper argues that once LLM applications retrieve external content, the boundary between data and instructions disappears, so an attacker can plant prompts in data the model will later read without ever talking to it directly. The authors build a security-oriented taxonomy of the resulting threats (data theft, worm-like spreading, contamination of the information ecosystem, among others) and demonstrate the attacks on deployed systems such as GPT-4-powered Bing Chat and code-completion tools as well as on synthetic GPT-4 applications. They show that retrieved prompts can behave like arbitrary code execution, steering application behaviour and which APIs get called.

- **Relevance:** Every handoff, envelope or tool result that crosses an agent boundary is retrieved content, so indirect prompt injection is the baseline threat any agent-movement protocol must contain.
- **Operations:** tool-access, identity-trust. **Contribution:** empirical. **Type:** workshop.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Seminal; arXiv title uses lower-case 'Not what you've signed up for'.

### AMP-031

Qiusi Zhan, Zhixiang Liang, Zifan Ying, Daniel Kang (2024). **InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents**. *Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024*. [doi:10.18653/v1/2024.findings-acl.624](https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2024.findings-acl.624). Cite key: `zhan2024injecagent`.

InjecAgent is a benchmark for indirect prompt injection against tool-integrated LLM agents, built from test cases that combine user tools with attacker tools and split attacker goals into direct harm to the user and exfiltration of private data. The authors evaluate 30 agents and find them broadly vulnerable; ReAct-prompted GPT-4 is compromised in roughly a quarter of cases, and reinforcing the injected instructions with a hacking prompt nearly doubles that rate.

- **Relevance:** Quantifies how content returned by tools can redirect an agent's actions, a key risk when work and context are passed between agents and tool servers.
- **Operations:** tool-access. **Contribution:** benchmark. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref.

### AMP-039

Edoardo Debenedetti, Jie Zhang, Mislav Balunović, Luca Beurer-Kellner, Marc Fischer, Florian Tramèr (2024). **AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents**. *Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37 (NeurIPS 2024), Datasets and Benchmarks Track*. [doi:10.52202/079017-2636](https://doi.org/10.52202/079017-2636). Cite key: `debenedetti2024agentdojo`.

AgentDojo is an extensible evaluation environment, rather than a fixed test set, for measuring how well tool-using LLM agents withstand prompt injections carried in tool outputs. It ships realistic task suites (e.g. email, e-banking, travel booking) with paired security test cases and implementations of attacks and defences from the literature, and supports adaptive attacks. The authors report that current models struggle with many tasks even without attack, and that existing injection attacks break some but not all security properties.

- **Relevance:** Provides the reference harness for testing whether an agent that receives delegated work and tool data can be hijacked, which a handoff or relocation layer would need to be evaluated against.
- **Operations:** tool-access. **Contribution:** benchmark. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** publisher. Note: Metadata from NeurIPS proceedings page (citation meta tags), Crossref and arXiv API. Proceedings DOI 10.52202/079017-2636, pp. 82895-82920.

### AMP-040

Hanrong Zhang, Jingyuan Huang, Kai Mei, Yifei Yao, Zhenting Wang, Chenlu Zhan, Hongwei Wang, Yongfeng Zhang (2025). **Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents**. *International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2025)*. [arXiv:2410.02644](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.02644). Cite key: `zhang2025agent`.

ASB is a framework that formalises and benchmarks attacks and defences against LLM agents across many scenarios, agents and tools. It covers prompt injection, memory poisoning, a new Plan-of-Thought backdoor and mixed attacks, together with corresponding defences, across multiple LLM backbones. Results show vulnerabilities at every stage of agent operation (system prompt, user prompt, tool use, memory retrieval) with high attack success and limited defence effectiveness, and the paper proposes a metric balancing utility and security.

- **Relevance:** Its memory-poisoning and stage-wise attack results show which parts of an agent's state are unsafe to carry across a handoff or checkpoint without integrity checks.
- **Operations:** tool-access, portable-context. **Contribution:** benchmark. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** publisher. Note: Venue confirmed on ICLR 2025 proceedings listing (proceedings.iclr.cc); authors and abstract from arXiv API.

### AMP-047

Zehang Deng, Yongjian Guo, Changzhou Han, Wanlun Ma, Junwu Xiong, Sheng Wen, Yang Xiang (2025). **AI Agents Under Threat: A Survey of Key Security Challenges and Future Pathways**. *ACM Computing Surveys, vol. 57, no. 7*. [doi:10.1145/3716628](https://doi.org/10.1145/3716628). Cite key: `deng2025ai`.

This survey systematises security threats to AI agents around four knowledge gaps: unpredictable multi-step user inputs, complex internal execution, variable operating environments, and interaction with untrusted external entities. It reviews attacks and defences under each gap, summarising progress and remaining limitations, and outlines directions for building more robust and secure agent applications.

- **Relevance:** Its category of interactions with untrusted external entities frames the threats that arise whenever an agent hands work to, or receives it from, another party.
- **Operations:** tool-access, identity-trust, governance. **Contribution:** survey. **Type:** journal.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Published online 2025-02-21; issue dated July 2025.

### AMP-049

Harold Triedman, Rishi Jha, Vitaly Shmatikov (2025). **Multi-Agent Systems Execute Arbitrary Malicious Code**. *Conference on Language Modeling (COLM 2025)*. [arXiv:2503.12188](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12188). Cite key: `triedman2025multi`.

Using several published multi-agent frameworks, the authors show that adversarial content such as malicious web pages or files can hijack the control and communication flow among agents so that the orchestrator invokes unsafe agents and capabilities. This can lead to arbitrary code execution on the user's device or exfiltration of data from a containerised environment; with GPT-4o, web-based attacks succeed in 58-90% of trials depending on the orchestrator, and reach 100% in some configurations. The attacks work even when individual agents resist direct and indirect prompt injection or refuse harmful actions.

- **Relevance:** Shows that orchestrator-to-sub-agent delegation is itself the exploitable channel, so security cannot be judged agent by agent but must cover the handoff graph.
- **Operations:** delegation, identity-trust. **Contribution:** empirical. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: Published at COLM 2025 (OpenReview DAozI4etUp); arXiv 2503.12188 first posted 2025-03-15. COLM version spells the second author 'Rishi Dev Jha'.

### AMP-062

Stav Cohen, Ron Bitton, Ben Nassi (2025). **Here Comes the AI Worm: Preventing the Propagation of Adversarial Self-Replicating Prompts Within GenAI Ecosystems**. *Proceedings of the 2025 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS '25)*. [doi:10.1145/3719027.3765196](https://doi.org/10.1145/3719027.3765196). Cite key: `cohen2025here`.

The paper shows that when GenAI-powered applications exchange messages and rely on RAG-based inference, an adversarial self-replicating prompt can start a worm-like chain of indirect prompt injections, called RAGworm, in which each compromised application acts maliciously and contaminates the retrieval stores of other applications. In an ecosystem of GenAI email assistants, the authors use it to promote content, spread propaganda and extract confidential data, and they report super-linear spread in which each infected client compromises about 20 others within one to three days. They also study which factors affect the worm's performance. Finally, they propose DonkeyRail, a guardrail that detects and stops propagation with a reported true-positive rate of 1.0, a false-positive rate of 0.017 and only milliseconds of added latency.

- **Relevance:** Demonstrates zero-click, multi-hop propagation of malicious context between agents, the worst case for any mechanism that forwards task context or memory between agents.
- **Operations:** delegation, portable-context, governance. **Contribution:** empirical. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: CCS '25 version, open access (CC BY). Its abstract names the worm 'RAGworm' and the guardrail 'DonkeyRail'. The earlier arXiv preprint 2403.02817 ('Here Comes The AI Worm: Unleashing Zero-click Worms that Target GenAI-Powered Applications') calls them 'Morris-II' and 'Virtual Donkey'. Semantic Scholar/DBLP (conf/ccs/CohenBN25) link the two; the summary follows the CCS abstract.

### AMP-064

Vineeth Sai Narajala, Idan Habler, Ken Huang, Prashant Kulkarni (2025). **Building A Secure Agentic AI Application Leveraging Google's A2A Protocol**. *2025 Annual Computer Security Applications Conference Workshops (ACSAC Workshops)*. [doi:10.1109/acsacw69556.2025.00043](https://doi.org/10.1109/acsacw69556.2025.00043). Cite key: `narajala2025building`.

The paper provides a security analysis of Google's Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, describing its components and operation in the context of agent communication. Using the MAESTRO AI threat-modelling framework, it identifies risks in A2A deployments, with emphasis on Agent Card management, task-execution integrity and authentication. It then recommends secure development practices and architectural patterns, and discusses how combining A2A with MCP can support secure interoperability.

- **Relevance:** One of the few peer-reviewed threat models of A2A and agent cards, the delegation protocol at the centre of the agent-movement study.
- **Operations:** delegation, identity-trust, tool-access, governance. **Contribution:** position. **Type:** workshop.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Author order and title differ across versions: arXiv lists Habler, Huang, Narajala, Kulkarni and omits "Google's"; the ACSAC Workshops version (Crossref) is used here. Crossref title uses a typographic apostrophe.

### AMP-068

Edoardo Debenedetti, Ilia Shumailov, Tianqi Fan, Jamie Hayes, Nicholas Carlini, Daniel Fabian, Christoph Kern, Chongyang Shi, Andreas Terzis, Florian Tramèr (2026). **Defeating Prompt Injections by Design**. *2026 IEEE Conference on Secure and Trustworthy Machine Learning (SaTML)*. [doi:10.1109/satml68715.2026.00040](https://doi.org/10.1109/satml68715.2026.00040). Cite key: `debenedetti2026defeating`.

CaMeL wraps an LLM agent in a protective system layer so that it stays secure even if the underlying model is susceptible to prompt injection. It derives the control and data flow from the trusted user query up front, so untrusted data retrieved later cannot change program flow, and attaches capabilities to values so security policies are enforced at tool-call time to block exfiltration over unauthorised flows. On AgentDojo it solves 77% of tasks with provable security versus 84% for an undefended system.

- **Relevance:** Capability-tagged data flows are a concrete design for carrying provenance and authorisation along with task context as it moves between agents and tools.
- **Operations:** tool-access, identity-trust, governance. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Preprint first posted March 2025; the SaTML 2026 proceedings version confirmed via Crossref.

### AMP-069

Zhiqiang Wang, Yichao Gao, Yanting Wang, Suyuan Liu, Haifeng Sun, Haoran Cheng, Guanquan Shi, Haohua Du, Xiangyang Li (2026). **MCPTox: A Benchmark for Tool Poisoning on Real-World MCP Servers**. *Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, vol. 40, no. 42 (AAAI-26)*. [doi:10.1609/aaai.v40i42.40895](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v40i42.40895). Cite key: `wang2026mcptox`.

MCPTox studies tool poisoning, where malicious instructions are hidden in an MCP tool's metadata rather than its outputs, and provides the first systematic benchmark for it, built on live real-world MCP servers and their tools with generated malicious test cases across ten risk categories. Evaluating 20 LLM agent settings, the authors find widespread vulnerability, with more capable models often more susceptible because the attack exploits instruction following, and agents almost never refuse.

- **Relevance:** Tool descriptions are part of what an agent ingests when it attaches to new tool servers after moving, so poisoned metadata is a direct risk for relocation and migration.
- **Operations:** tool-access, identity-trust. **Contribution:** benchmark. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: arXiv title is 'MCPTox: A Benchmark for Tool Poisoning Attack on Real-World MCP Servers'; AAAI title omits 'Attack'.

### AMP-072

Donghyun Lee, Mo Tiwari, Brando Miranda (2026). **Prompt Infection: LLM-to-LLM Prompt Injection within Multi-agent Systems**. *Computer Security. ESORICS 2025 International Workshops, Lecture Notes in Computer Science (Springer)*. [doi:10.1007/978-3-032-16092-8_28](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-16092-8_28). Cite key: `lee2026prompt`.

The paper shows that prompt injection can spread between LLM agents in a multi-agent system: an injected prompt copies itself from agent to agent, so the attack moves through the system like a computer virus. This adds data propagation and self-replication to ordinary prompt injection, and it can enable data theft, scams, misinformation and system-wide disruption. The published version reports that existing prompt-injection defenses, adapted for multi-agent use, reduce how far the infection spreads. The earlier arXiv preprint frames its defense as LLM Tagging, which marks agent-originated messages, used together with existing safeguards.

- **Relevance:** Models the risk that a message delegated from one agent to another carries a self-replicating injection, which motivates provenance marking and injection defenses on every inter-agent handoff.
- **Operations:** delegation, identity-trust. **Contribution:** empirical. **Type:** workshop.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Published version (Crossref, Springer LNCS 16232, pp. 511-520, online 2026-05-01) adds a third author, Brando Miranda, who is not in arXiv v1 (Lee, Tiwari). The abstracts differ: the published one credits repurposed existing prompt-injection defenses, while arXiv v1 proposes LLM Tagging.

### AMP-073

John T. Halloran, Brandon Radosevich, Gavin Black (2026). **MCP safety audit: LLMs with the model context protocol allow major security exploits**. *Assurance and Security for AI-enabled Systems 2026 (Proceedings of SPIE)*. [doi:10.1117/12.3097390](https://doi.org/10.1117/12.3097390). Cite key: `halloran2026mcp`.

The paper argues that the MCP design exposes end users to serious risks and demonstrates that leading LLMs can be induced, through MCP tools, to compromise a developer's machine via malicious code execution, remote access control and credential theft. As a mitigation it introduces MCPSafetyScanner, an agentic auditing tool that generates adversarial samples from an MCP server's tools and resources, searches for related vulnerabilities and remediations, and produces a security report before deployment.

- **Relevance:** Shows that the tool-access layer agents rely on after a handoff or relocation is itself an attack vector and offers a pre-deployment audit approach for MCP servers.

Halloran, Brandon Radosevich, Gavin Black. SPIE conference proceedings; review depth may be lighter than for archival conferences.

This study examines MCP from architectural and security perspectives, defining an MCP server lifecycle of four phases (creation, deployment, operation, maintenance) broken into 16 activities. On that basis it builds a threat taxonomy across four attacker types (malicious developers, external attackers, malicious users and security flaws) covering 16 threat scenarios, validated with real-world case studies. It then proposes phase- and threat-specific safeguards and surveys MCP adoption and tooling to identify limitations and research directions.

## P4: Agent identity, delegated authorization, accountability and governance

### AMP-002

Butler Lampson, Martín Abadi, Michael Burrows, Edward Wobber (1992). **Authentication in Distributed Systems: Theory and Practice**. *ACM Transactions on Computer Systems, 10(4), 265-310*. [doi:10.1145/138873.138874](https://doi.org/10.1145/138873.138874). Cite key: `lampson1992authentication`.

Presents a theory of authentication built on principals and a 'speaks for' relation, where compound principals can express adopted roles or delegated authority, and shows how to reason about a principal's authority by deducing whom it speaks for. The theory is used to explain many security mechanisms and a built system that passes principals through RPCs and handles encryption, naming, groups, program loading, delegation, access control and revocation.

- **Relevance:** The speaks-for calculus is the classic formal basis for reasoning about chains of delegated authority, as in agent-to-agent handoffs.
- **Operations:** delegation, identity-trust. **Contribution:** formal. **Type:** journal.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Crossref splits title/subtitle ('Authentication in distributed systems' / 'theory and practice'). An earlier version appeared at SOSP 1991 (DOI 10.1145/121132.121160).

### AMP-016

Arnar Birgisson, Joe Gibbs Politz, Úlfar Erlingsson, Ankur Taly, Michael Vrable, Mark Lentczner (2014). **Macaroons: Cookies with Contextual Caveats for Decentralized Authorization in the Cloud**. *Proceedings 2014 Network and Distributed System Security Symposium (NDSS 2014)*. [doi:10.14722/ndss.2014.23212](https://doi.org/10.14722/ndss.2014.23212). Cite key: `birgisson2014macaroons`.

Introduces macaroons, authorization credentials as cheap and deployable as web cookies thanks to a chained-HMAC construction. Unlike cookies, holders can attenuate and delegate them in a decentralized way by adding contextual caveats, giving expressiveness comparable to public-key mechanisms such as SPKI/SDSI while confining how, by whom and in what context authority is exercised.

- **Relevance:** Attenuable, chainable credentials are a natural primitive for passing narrowed authority along a chain of delegated agents.
- **Operations:** delegation, identity-trust. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Date 22 Feb 2014 from the NDSS publisher page; Crossref gives year 2014 only.

[doi:10.1145/2976749.2978385](https://doi.org/10.1145/2976749.2978385). Cite key: `fett2016comprehensive`.

Performs the first extensive formal analysis of the OAuth 2.0 standard in an expressive web model, with formal definitions of authorization, authentication and session-integrity properties. The analysis covers all four grant types running concurrently with malicious relying parties, identity providers and browsers. In the course of the proof the authors found four practical attacks on OAuth (also present in OpenID Connect), proposed fixes, and proved security of the fixed protocol in their model.

- **Relevance:** OAuth is the base most agent-delegation proposals extend, so its formally established guarantees and pitfalls bound what agent-delegation schemes can claim.

## P5: Agent memory, state, context and durable execution

### AMP-019

Athinagoras Skiadopoulos, Qian Li, Peter Kraft, Kostis Kaffes, Daniel Hong, Shana Mathew, David Bestor, Michael Cafarella, Vijay Gadepally, Goetz Graefe, Jeremy Kepner, Christos Kozyrakis, Tim Kraska, Michael Stonebraker, Lalith Suresh, Matei Zaharia (2021). **DBOS: A DBMS-oriented Operating System**. *Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment, vol. 15, no. 1, pp. 21-30*. [doi:10.14778/3485450.3485454](https://doi.org/10.14778/3485450.3485454). Cite key: `skiadopoulos2021dbos`.

The authors argue that a distributed transactional DBMS, rather than a single-node OS plus separate cluster services, should be the foundation of a scalable cluster operating system. Their DBOS prototype implements scheduling, file management and inter-process communication as database operations with competitive performance, while gaining better analytics, less code, and transactions and high availability implemented once.

- **Relevance:** Putting all execution state in a transactional database is the basis of the durable-execution approach that lets workflows, including agent workflows, resume on another machine after failure.
- **Operations:** runtime-relocation, observability. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** journal.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Crossref stores the title only as 'DBOS'; the full title is taken from the paper. PVLDB vol. 15 is dated 2021-09 by Crossref and is associated with VLDB 2022. Concerns durable state management in general, not LLM agents specifically.

### AMP-022

Charles Packer, Sarah Wooders, Kevin Lin, Vivian Fang, Shishir G. Patil, Ion Stoica, Joseph E. Gonzalez (2023). **MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems**. *arXiv preprint*. [arXiv:2310.08560](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560). Cite key: `packer2023memgpt`.

Fixed context windows limit LLMs in long conversations and large-document analysis. MemGPT borrows the OS idea of hierarchical memory, letting the LLM page information between a bounded in-context store and external storage tiers, and uses interrupts to manage control flow with the user. The authors evaluate it on document analysis beyond the context window and on multi-session chat where agents retain and evolve memory over long interactions.

- **Relevance:** Externalizing agent state into explicit memory tiers is a prerequisite for packaging that state into a portable context and resuming an agent elsewhere.
- **Operations:** portable-context, runtime-relocation. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** preprint (not peer reviewed).

### AMP-023

Sheng Qi, Xuanzhe Liu, Xin Jin (2023). **Halfmoon: Log-Optimal Fault-Tolerant Stateful Serverless Computing**. *Proceedings of the 29th ACM Symposium on Operating Systems Principles (SOSP '23)*. [doi:10.1145/3600006.3613154](https://doi.org/10.1145/3600006.3613154). Cite key: `qi2023halfmoon`.

Retrying failed serverless functions can apply duplicate updates to shared external state, and current log-based fixes for exactly-once semantics log every read and write. Halfmoon shows that logging only reads or only writes suffices, and gives two protocols that it proves are log-optimal, with a criterion and a pauseless mechanism for switching between them. The prototype reports lower latency and lower logging overhead than the prior system Boki.

- **Relevance:** Exactly-once handling of side effects on retry is the core correctness problem when an agent run is resumed or replayed on a different worker after a crash.
- **Operations:** runtime-relocation. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.

Each agent keeps a natural-language memory stream of its experiences, periodically synthesizes it into higher-level reflections, and retrieves relevant memories to plan. LLM applications and agents chain many LLM requests, but public LLM services only see individual requests and optimize them blindly. Gonzalez, Ion Stoica (2025). **Autellix: An Efficient Serving Engine for LLM Agents as General Programs**. *arXiv preprint*. [arXiv:2502.13965](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13965). Cite key: `luo2025autellix`.

Agentic programs issue many dependent LLM calls, but serving engines treat calls independently and suffer head-of-line blocking at both the request and program level. Autellix intercepts the calls, gives the scheduler program-level context, and introduces scheduling algorithms for single-threaded and distributed programs that preempt and prioritize calls based on the program's completed work. The authors report 4-15x higher program throughput at equal latency compared with systems such as vLLM.

- **Relevance:** Treating an agent program, rather than an individual call, as the unit the serving layer tracks and places across engines is directly relevant to relocating agent execution between machines.

The paper argues that LLM uncertainty and cost create reliability, privacy, cost and performance problems for agents, and proposes AgentRR, which brings classical record-and-replay into agent frameworks. [doi:10.3233/FAIA251160](https://doi.org/10.3233/FAIA251160). Cite key: `chhikara2025mem`.

Mem0 is a memory layer for LLM agents that extracts the salient facts from ongoing multi-session conversations, consolidates them and retrieves them later; a variant stores memories as a graph to capture relations between entities. On the LOCOMO benchmark the authors compare it with six baseline categories, including memory-augmented systems, RAG setups, full-context prompting and commercial memory products. Mem0 outperforms the existing memory systems across single-hop, temporal, multi-hop and open-domain questions. Full-context prompting stays slightly more accurate, but Mem0 cuts p95 latency by about 91% and token cost by over 90% compared with it.

- **Relevance:** Shows that persistent, externalized memory can be a service decoupled from any single model or session, which is what lets context survive movement between agents and runtimes.
- **Operations:** portable-context. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Crossref types the record as a book-chapter in the IOS Press FAIA series; it is the ECAI 2025 proceedings paper.

### AMP-063

Wujiang Xu, Zujie Liang, Kai Mei, Hang Gao, Juntao Tan, Yongfeng Zhang (2025). **A-Mem: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents**. *Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38 (NeurIPS 2025)*. [doi:10.52202/085713-0593](https://doi.org/10.52202/085713-0593). Cite key: `xu2025mem`.

Existing agent memory systems offer basic storage and retrieval with fixed structures and operations. A-Mem lets the agent organize memory itself following Zettelkasten principles: each new memory becomes a structured note with context, keywords and tags, is linked to related past notes, and can trigger updates to existing notes so the memory network evolves. Experiments across six foundation models report improvements over prior state-of-the-art baselines.

- **Relevance:** Self-organizing, linked memory is a candidate format for agent state that must remain coherent when transferred or merged between agents.
- **Operations:** portable-context. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: NeurIPS 2025 acceptance confirmed via arXiv comment and OpenReview (NeurIPS 2025 poster, note FiM0M8gcct). Proceedings DOI 10.52202/085713-0593 (NeurIPS 38, pp. 20004-20031) per Crossref. Proceedings title uses 'A-Mem'; arXiv uses 'A-MEM'. date_published approximates the conference month.

### AMP-071

Qizheng Zhang, Changran Hu, Shubhangi Upasani, Boyuan Ma, Fenglu Hong, Vamsidhar Kamanuru, Jay Rainton, Chen Wu, Mengmeng Ji, Hanchen Li, Urmish Thakker, James Zou, Kunle Olukotun (2026). **Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models**. *International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2026)*. [arXiv:2510.04618](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04618). Cite key: `zhang2026agentic`.

Adapting LLM applications by rewriting their contexts suffers from brevity bias and from context collapse, where repeated rewriting erodes detail. ACE treats contexts as evolving playbooks maintained through generation, reflection and curation, applying structured incremental updates instead of full rewrites. It improves over strong baselines on agent and finance benchmarks in both offline (system prompt) and online (agent memory) settings while lowering adaptation latency and cost, and can learn from execution feedback without labels.

- **Relevance:** Treats the agent's context as a structured, incrementally updated artifact, which is the form a portable task context needs in order to be carried and extended by successive agents.
- **Operations:** portable-context. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: ICLR 2026 acceptance confirmed via arXiv comment and OpenReview (venue 'ICLR 2026 Poster'). No DOI. date_published approximates the conference month.

### AMP-074

Minki Kang, Wei-Ning Chen, Dongge Han, Huseyin A. Inan, Lukas Wutschitz, Yanzhi Chen, Robert Sim, Saravan Rajmohan (2026). **ACON: Optimizing Context Compression for Long-horizon LLM Agents**. *International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026)*. [arXiv:2510.00615](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.00615). Cite key: `kang2026acon`.

Long-horizon agents accumulate unbounded histories that raise inference memory cost and degrade reasoning. ACON compresses both observations and interaction history by iteratively refining natural-language compression guidelines from analysis of agent failures, without fine-tuning the agent, and then distils the compressor into smaller models. On AppWorld, OfficeBench and multi-objective QA it reduces peak token usage by 26-54% while improving task success over compression baselines.

- **Relevance:** Compressing agent history while preserving critical state is exactly the problem of producing a compact, transferable task context for handoff or resumption.
- **Operations:** portable-context. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: ICML 2026 acceptance confirmed via arXiv comment and OpenReview (venue 'ICML 2026 regular'). No DOI. date_published approximates the conference month.


## P6: Multi-agent orchestration, delegation and portable agent specifications

### AMP-001

Reid G. Smith (1980). **The Contract Net Protocol: High-Level Communication and Control in a Distributed Problem Solver**. *IEEE Transactions on Computers, vol. C-29, no. 12, pp. 1104-1113*. [doi:10.1109/TC.1980.1675516](https://doi.org/10.1109/TC.1980.1675516). Cite key: `smith1980contract`.

Addresses how a network of loosely coupled problem-solving nodes can distribute tasks among themselves without central control. It specifies the contract net protocol, in which a manager announces a task, potential contractors submit bids, and the manager awards a contract, with nodes able to take manager or contractor roles dynamically. The paper presents the message types and negotiation structure as a general high-level communication and control mechanism for distributed problem solvers.

- **Relevance:** The canonical announce-bid-award delegation protocol that modern agent-to-agent task handoff (e.g. A2A task negotiation) implicitly re-creates.
- **Operations:** delegation. **Contribution:** formal. **Type:** journal.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref. Note: Crossref lists only the family name 'Smith'; full name 'Reid G. Smith' confirmed from the paper's title page (author-hosted PDF). Summary checked against the full text, which also demonstrates the protocol on a distributed-sensing problem.

### AMP-020

Guohao Li, Hasan Abed Al Kader Hammoud, Hani Itani, Dmitrii Khizbullin, Bernard Ghanem (2023). **CAMEL: Communicative Agents for "Mind" Exploration of Large Language Model Society**. *Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36 (NeurIPS 2023)*. [arXiv:2303.17760](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17760). Cite key: `li2023camel`.

Asks how chat-based LLM agents can cooperate autonomously on complex tasks without continuous human steering. The authors propose a role-playing framework in which inception prompting keeps an instructing agent and an executing agent on task and aligned with human intent. They use it to generate conversational data for studying the cooperative behaviour of agent societies and release an open-source library.

- **Relevance:** An early instructor-executor delegation pattern between LLM agents, illustrating how task intent must be preserved as work passes from one agent to another.
- **Operations:** delegation. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: arXiv comment states 'Accepted at NeurIPS 2023'; confirmed via OpenReview API (NeurIPS 2023 poster). arXiv first posted 2023-03-31.

### AMP-021

Yongliang Shen, Kaitao Song, Xu Tan, Dongsheng Li, Weiming Lu, Yueting Zhuang (2023). **HuggingGPT: Solving AI Tasks with ChatGPT and its Friends in Hugging Face**. *Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36 (NeurIPS 2023)*. [doi:10.52202/075280-1657](https://doi.org/10.52202/075280-1657). Cite key: `shen2023hugginggpt`.

Proposes using an LLM as a controller that orchestrates many specialist AI models, with language as the common interface. HuggingGPT has ChatGPT plan a user request into subtasks, select models from Hugging Face based on their textual function descriptions, execute each subtask with the chosen model, and summarize the results. The authors report that this approach handles a broad range of language, vision, speech and cross-modal tasks.

- **Relevance:** A canonical planner-to-specialist delegation loop where capability descriptions drive routing, the same pattern used by agent cards and capability discovery in delegation protocols.
- **Operations:** delegation, tool-access. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: Venue confirmed via OpenReview (NeurIPS 2023 poster). Proceedings DOI 10.52202/075280-1657 (NeurIPS 36, pp. 38154-38180) per Crossref. arXiv first posted 2023-03-30.

### AMP-027

Weize Chen, Yusheng Su, Jingwei Zuo, Cheng Yang, Chenfei Yuan, Chi-Min Chan, Heyang Yu, Yaxi Lu, Yi-Hsin Hung, Chen Qian, Yujia Qin, Xin Cong, Ruobing Xie, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun, Jie Zhou (2024). **AgentVerse: Facilitating Multi-Agent Collaboration and Exploring Emergent Behaviors**. *International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2024)*. [arXiv:2308.10848](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.10848). Cite key: `chen2024agentverse`.

Motivated by human group dynamics, the paper proposes AgentVerse, a multi-agent framework that dynamically adjusts the composition of an agent group while it works on a task. Experiments indicate that the resulting groups outperform a single agent. The authors also examine emergent social behaviours among agents during collaboration and discuss strategies to amplify helpful behaviours and curb harmful ones.

- **Relevance:** Dynamic recruitment and re-composition of agent teams is a form of runtime delegation in which work and context move between changing sets of agents.
- **Operations:** delegation. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: Venue confirmed via OpenReview API (ICLR 2024 poster). arXiv first posted 2023-08-21.

### AMP-028

Qingyun Wu, Gagan Bansal, Jieyu Zhang, Yiran Wu, Beibin Li, Erkang Zhu, Li Jiang, Xiaoyun Zhang, Shaokun Zhang, Jiale Liu, Ahmed Hassan Awadallah, Ryen W White, Doug Burger, Chi Wang (2024). **AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversations**. *Conference on Language Modeling (COLM 2024)*. [arXiv:2308.08155](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155). Cite key: `wu2024autogen`.

Proposes AutoGen, an open-source framework in which LLM applications are built from multiple customizable, conversable agents that can combine LLMs, human input and tools. Interaction behaviours between agents are programmed through conversation patterns expressed in natural language and code. The authors present example applications spanning mathematics, coding, question answering, operations research, online decision-making and entertainment to show the framework's generality.

- **Relevance:** AutoGen's conversation-based agent-to-agent handoff is one of the dominant framework-specific delegation models that cross-framework movement must bridge.
- **Operations:** delegation, tool-access. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: arXiv v2 title ends 'Multi-Agent Conversation'; the COLM 2024 version (OpenReview BAakY1hNKS) is titled '...Multi-Agent Conversations'. Venue confirmed via OpenReview API; arXiv first posted 2023-08-16.

### AMP-029

Chen Qian, Wei Liu, Hongzhang Liu, Nuo Chen, Yufan Dang, Jiahao Li, Cheng Yang, Weize Chen, Yusheng Su, Xin Cong, Juyuan Xu, Dahai Li, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun (2024). **ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development**. *Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), pp. 15174-15186*. [doi:10.18653/v1/2024.acl-long.810](https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2024.acl-long.810). Cite key: `qian2024chatdev`.

Argues that phase-specific deep-learning models fragment the software development process. ChatDev instead has specialized LLM agents carry out design, coding and testing, using a chat chain to decide what is communicated at each phase and communicative dehallucination to govern how. The authors find natural language useful for system design and programming language useful for debugging, positioning language as a unifying bridge for multi-agent task solving.

- **Relevance:** Its phase-by-phase chat chain is an explicit sequential handoff structure whose context passing between roles is a concrete instance of agent-to-agent work transfer.
- **Operations:** delegation, portable-context. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** crossref.

### AMP-030

Omar Khattab, Arnav Singhvi, Paridhi Maheshwari, Zhiyuan Zhang, Keshav Santhanam, Sri Vardhamanan, Saiful Haq, Ashutosh Sharma, Thomas T. Joshi, Hanna Moazam, Heather Miller, Matei Zaharia, Christopher Potts (2024). **DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into State-of-the-Art Pipelines**. *International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2024), spotlight*. [arXiv:2310.03714](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.03714). Cite key: `khattab2024dspy`.

Criticizes LM pipelines built from hand-tuned prompt strings and introduces DSPy, a programming model that expresses pipelines as text-transformation graphs whose LM calls are declarative, parameterized modules. A compiler optimizes any DSPy program against a target metric by bootstrapping demonstrations. Case studies on math word problems, multi-hop retrieval, complex QA and agent loops show compiled programs beating standard few-shot prompting and expert-written demonstrations, including on smaller open models.

- **Relevance:** Separating a declarative pipeline specification from model-specific prompts is a key enabler for moving agent logic across models without rewriting it.
- **Operations:** cross-framework-migration, portable-context. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: arXiv v1 title ends 'into Self-Improving Pipelines'; ICLR 2024 version (OpenReview sY5N0zY5Od, spotlight) ends 'into State-of-the-Art Pipelines'. OpenReview lists 'Sri Vardhamanan A'. arXiv first posted 2023-10-05.

### AMP-032

Sirui Hong, Mingchen Zhuge, Jiaqi Chen, Xiawu Zheng, Yuheng Cheng, Ceyao Zhang, Jinlin Wang, Zili Wang, Steven Ka Shing Yau, Zijuan Lin, Liyang Zhou, Chenyu Ran, Lingfeng Xiao, Chenglin Wu, Jürgen Schmidhuber (2024). **MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework**. *International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2024), oral*. [arXiv:2308.00352](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352). Cite key: `hong2024metagpt`.

Targets the logic inconsistencies and cascading hallucinations that arise when LLM agents are naively chained. MetaGPT encodes human Standardized Operating Procedures into prompt sequences and arranges role-specialized agents in an assembly-line paradigm, with structured intermediate outputs that other agents can verify. On collaborative software-engineering benchmarks it is reported to produce more coherent solutions than earlier chat-based multi-agent systems.

- **Relevance:** Shows that handoffs between agents work better when the transferred work product is a structured, verifiable artifact rather than free chat, a key design input for a portable task envelope.
- **Operations:** delegation, portable-context. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: Venue confirmed via OpenReview API (VtmBAGCN7o, ICLR 2024 oral); OpenReview lists the third author as 'Jonathan Chen', arXiv as 'Jiaqi Chen'. arXiv first posted 2023-08-01.

### AMP-037

Taicheng Guo, Xiuying Chen, Yaqi Wang, Ruidi Chang, Shichao Pei, Nitesh V. Chawla, Olaf Wiest, Xiangliang Zhang (2024). **Large Language Model Based Multi-agents: A Survey of Progress and Challenges**. *Proceedings of the Thirty-Third International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI 2024), pp. 8048-8057*. [doi:10.24963/ijcai.2024/890](https://doi.org/10.24963/ijcai.2024/890). Cite key: `guo2024large`.

Surveys the rapidly growing field of LLM-based multi-agent systems used for problem solving and world simulation. It organizes the literature around the domains and environments agents simulate, how agents are profiled, how they communicate, and which mechanisms grow their capabilities. ### AMP-042

Mert Cemri, Melissa Z. Pan, Shuyi Yang, Lakshya A. Agrawal, Bhavya Chopra, Rishabh Tiwari, Kurt Keutzer, Aditya Parameswaran, Dan Klein, Kannan Ramchandran, Matei Zaharia, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Ion Stoica (2025). **Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?**. *Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38 (NeurIPS 2025), Datasets and Benchmarks Track*. [arXiv:2503.13657](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.13657). Cite key: `cemri2025do`.

Starts from the observation that multi-agent LLM systems often deliver minimal gains on benchmarks and sets out to explain why. The authors annotate execution traces from seven popular frameworks, building the MAST-Data dataset and the Multi-Agent System Failure Taxonomy (MAST), whose 14 failure modes fall into system design issues, inter-agent misalignment and task verification. They add an LLM-as-a-Judge annotator that agrees well with human labels and use it to analyse failures across models and tasks.

- **Relevance:** Inter-agent misalignment failures such as lost context and ignored inputs are exactly the risks a disciplined handoff and portable task envelope must prevent, and MAST offers a vocabulary for observing them.
- **Operations:** delegation, observability. **Contribution:** taxonomy. **Type:** conference.
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: Peer-reviewed version confirmed via OpenReview API as NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks Track (spotlight); also appeared as a NeurIPS 2025 LLM Evaluation Workshop poster. arXiv first posted 2025-03-17.

### AMP-059

Soufiane Amini, Yassine Benajiba, Cesare Bernardis, Paul Cayet, Hassan Chafi, Abderrahim Fathan, Louis Faucon, Damien Hilloulin, Sungpack Hong, Ingo Kossyk, Tran Minh Son Le, Rhicheek Patra, Sujith Ravi, Jonas Schweizer, Jyotika Singh, Shailender Singh, Weiyi Sun, Kartik Talamadupula, Jerry Xu (2025). **Open Agent Specification (Agent Spec): A Unified Representation for AI Agents**. *arXiv preprint*. [arXiv:2510.04173](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04173). Cite key: `amini2025open`.

Responds to fragmentation across agent frameworks, which differ in abstractions, data-flow semantics and tool integration, by proposing Agent Spec, a declarative language for defining agents and agentic workflows once and running them on different runtimes. It defines shared components, control- and data-flow semantics and schemas, plus a standardized evaluation harness for comparing behaviour across runtimes. The authors demonstrate it on four runtimes (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, WayFlow) over three benchmarks and release an SDK, reference runtime and framework adapters.

- **Relevance:** The most direct attempt at a framework-neutral agent representation, which is the prerequisite for cross-framework migration of agents and workflows.
- **Operations:** cross-framework-migration, portable-context, observability. **Contribution:** system. **Type:** preprint (not peer reviewed).
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: Author list from arXiv v4 (current); an earlier technical-report version indexed by DBLP/OpenReview has a different author list (e.g. includes Vladislav Blinov, Xuelin Situ, Ying Xu). No peer-reviewed version found.

### AMP-067

Nenad Tomašev, Matija Franklin, Simon Osindero (2026). **Intelligent AI Delegation**. *arXiv preprint*. [arXiv:2602.11865](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11865). Cite key: `tomasev2026intelligent`.

Argues that current task decomposition and delegation among AI agents rely on simple heuristics that cannot adapt to changing environments or robustly handle failures. The authors propose an adaptive framework that treats delegation as a sequence of decisions covering task allocation together with transfer of authority, responsibility and accountability, explicit role and boundary specifications, clarity of intent, and trust-establishment mechanisms. The framework is meant to apply to human and AI delegators and delegatees in delegation networks and to inform protocols for the emerging agentic web.

- **Relevance:** Frames delegation as the transfer of authority and accountability, not just a task, which is precisely what an accountable agent handoff must carry.
- **Operations:** delegation, identity-trust, governance. **Contribution:** position. **Type:** preprint (not peer reviewed).
- **Metadata verified via:** arxiv. Note: No peer-reviewed version found via OpenReview search as of 2026-10-15.
